newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police close file on Jerusalem shooting.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police close file on Jerusalem shooting.

text.p: An Israeli inquiry into the killing of three Arab protesters at Jerusalem's al-Aqsa mosque in September has found that Israeli police used "excessive force" but the file was closed because the perpetrators could not be identified.

The justice ministry said in a statement faxed to Reuters on Friday that investigators found that some policemen had fired rubber bullets from close range but could not determine who caused the casualties.

"It emerged in the investigation that during the event at times there was excessive use of force without any need towards people on the Temple Mount and some cases of firing rubber bullets unjustifiably and from a forbidden range," the statement said.
"From the entire findings of the inquiry it was not possible to identify the individual shooter whose gun caused the casualties. Therefore there was no choice but to close the file," it said.
Police spokesmen declined to comment on the report.

Palestinians have charged that Israeli police used live ammunition and rubber bullets when they stormed al-Aqsa mosque compound to quell a demonstration against Israel's opening of a tourist tunnel near Islam's third holiest shrine. At least 50 Palestinians were wounded during the violence.
Israel said at the time that police acted after protesters hurled rocks over a wall at Jewish worshippers praying at the Western Wall.

The demonstration came after gun battles between Israeli soldiers and Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) police in the West Bank and Gaza Strip over the tunnel. A total of 61 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed in the clashes.
The justice ministry statement said the investigation results will be transferred to the police to draw the proper conclusions.
On Friday, more than 250,000 Palestinians packed al-Aqsa mosque compound for prayers marking the last Friday of the holy month of Ramadan, Israeli police said.
They said that prayers ended peacefully. Israel Radio said that about 2,500 policemen were deployed throughout Arab East Jerusalem to prevent possible demonstrations during and after the prayers.
